labelMismatches.reason: The actual question concerns named competent human oversight and the ability to disregard, override, reverse or stop an output. A synthetic identity-bound decision for one benefit case tests only part of that scope.

The notice question does not itself require a particular caseworker decision. The deep question also requires deployer-controlled logs retained for six months; a case decision and notice fixture does not prove that retention.

A machine can check the six declared elements, reviewer-reference presence, notification evidence and order of dates. It cannot assess the FRIA content, establish lawful applicability or supply a human assessor.
A canary egress fixture does not establish the full vendor contract, agency consent, model and data portability, knowledge transfer, licensing, pricing or an exercised exit plan.
A timely route to an authorized human tests delivery and authority only. It does not establish the substantive explanation of the actual decision, legal eligibility or the contents of the response.
The question includes WCAG 2.1 AA, channel coverage, keyboard focus and an accessibility statement. The later WCAG output check is a pending dependency, not evidence for that complete scope.
The question separates federal Section 508 WCAG 2.0 A/AA from state and local ADA duties. A generic later WCAG check does not establish equivalence, jurisdiction, dates or those legal duties.

These questions require deployer disclosure and may include editorial responsibility or first-interaction notice. Machine-readable marking alone does not establish disclosure, its exception or every channel notice.
Accountability, an oversight rationale, separation of recommendations from final decisions and a bidder contest route require document and human review. No simulator substitutes for those records.
